text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Friday.
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index powered to its third record close of the week as gilts extended Thursday's sharp gains and Wall Street advanced.
Ending above 4,200 for the first time ever, the index closed 10.2 points higher at 4,207.7 for a rise of 151.10 on the week.
FRANKFURT - Germany's blue chip DAX index ended bourse trade above the magical 3,000-point level, boosted by a 30-month record high for the dollar, but held off further gains by low volumes.
The 30-share DAX ended bourse trade at 3,001.37 points, up 8.06 points and up 67.98 on the week. In post-bourse trade the index rose 10.75 to 3,006.87.
PARIS - French shares closed at a fresh historic record close, just below an alltime intra-day trading high, as the market continued its bull run fuelled by fresh liquidity and a firmer dollar.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 17.33 points at 2,425.10. The index gained 97.6 points this week.

ZURICH - Swiss shares again ended at a record high as the dollar's gains propelled prices higher. Demand focused on industrial shares, which tend to benefit from a stronger dollar, while banks were neglected.
The Broad Swiss Performance Index ended up 10.31 points at a record high of 2,579.26 for a jump of 52.65 on the week.
TOKYO - Tokyo stocks closed slightly lower as early gains mainly prompted by buying back in the construction sector lost momentum.
The Nikkei 225 average, which rose over 300 points early in the afternoon, ended down 54.30 points at 18,090.04 for a gain of 786.49 on the week.
HONG KONG - The Hang Seng index capped a record-breaking week with its third consecutive all-time closing high, with gains in the banking sector offsetting profit-taking among property counters.
The index rose 25.72 points to close at 13,856.40, up 664.90 from last Friday's close.
SYDNEY - A dull Australian share market ambled to a flat finish, the big banks bolstering a soft industrial sector while miners saw recent gains trimmed.
The All Ordinaries index lost just 0.8 points to 2,435.5 for a gain of 16.9 on the week.
JOHANNESBURG - South African shares finished more or less flat after what dealers called a "rest" day following a busy week.

The all-share index was up 3.9 points to 6,782.9 for a gain of 108.3 from last Friday. The industrial index rose 4.0 points to 8,180.4, up 141.1 on the week, and golds added 5.2 points to 1,426.2 for a gain of 4.4 from last week's close.
